Background Recent data have shown that γδ T cells can act as mediators for immune defense against tumors. Our previous study has demonstrated that persisting clonally expanded TRDV4 T cells might be relatively beneficial for the outcome of patients with T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). However, little is known about the distribution and clonality of the TRDV repertoire in T cell receptor (TCR) of γδ T cells and their effects on the clinical outcome of patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The aim of this study was to assess whether the oligoclonal expansion of TCR V δ T cells could be used as an immune biomarker for AML outcome. Findings γδ T cells were sorted from the peripheral blood of 30 patients with untreated AML and 12 healthy donors. The complementarity-determining region 3 (CDR3) sizes of eight TCR V δ subfamily genes ( TRDV1 to TRDV8 ) were analyzed in sorted γδ T cells using RT-PCR and GeneScan. The most frequently expressed TRDV subfamilies in the AML patients were TRDV8 (86.67 %) and TRDV 2 (83.33 %), and the frequencies for TRDV1 , TRDV3 , TRDV4 , and TRDV6 were significantly lower than those in healthy individuals. The most frequent clonally expanded TRDV subfamilies in the AML patients included TRDV8 (56.67 %) and TRDV4 (40 %). The clonal expansion frequencies of the TRDV2 and TRDV4 T cells were significantly higher than those in healthy individuals, whereas a significantly lower TRDV1 clonal expansion frequency was observed in those with AML. Moreover, the oligoclones of TRDV4 and TRDV8 were independent protective factors for complete remission. Furthermore, the oligoclonal expansion frequencies of TRDV5 and TRDV6 in patients with relapse were significantly higher than those in non-recurrent cases. Conclusions To the best of our knowledge, we characterized for the first time a significant alteration in the distribution and clonality of the TRDV subfamily members in γδ T cells sorted from AML patients. Clonally expanded TRDV4 and TRDV8 T cells might contribute to the immune response directed against AML, while oligoclonal TRDV5 and TRDV6 might occur in patients who undergo relapse. While the function of such γδ T cell clones requires further investigation, TRDV γδ T cell clones might be potential immune biomarkers for AML outcome. extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the distribution and clonality of the TRDV repertoire within γδ T cells in peripheral blood from acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, comparing them to healthy individuals. The aim was to determine if oligoclonal expansion of TCR Vδ T cells could serve as an immune biomarker for AML outcome. Findings revealed significant alterations in TRDV subfamily member distribution and clonality, with clonally expanded TRDV4 and TRDV8 T cells identified as potential protective factors for complete remission, while oligoclonal TRDV5 and TRDV6 T cells were associated with AML recurrence.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Investigation of immunological and prognostic biomarkers for Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) outcome
treatment_details.dose_specificity: No therapeutic intervention or dose was administered. The study involved analyzing endogenous biomarker levels from sorted peripheral blood γδ T cells/PBMCs in 30 untreated AML patients and 12 healthy donors, using RT-PCR and GeneScan to assess gene transcript clonality and expression of eight TRDV subfamily genes (TRDV1-TRDV8). Comparisons were made between AML patients, healthy individuals, and within AML patients based on complete remission status and recurrence, with no dose-response comparisons.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Frequencies and clonal expansion frequencies were significantly lower in AML patients compared to healthy individuals (P=0.000 for expression, P=0.046 for clonal expansion), with oligoclonal expansion observed in 6.67% of AML patients.
